name: North Sulawesi Flash Floods
scale: Multiple rivers overtopping, widespread inundation
description: Flash flooding struck North Sulawesi province on 5 January, killing at least 16 people. The floods were triggered by intense rainfall that overwhelmed river channels across the region.

name: Mayon Volcano Eruption
scale: Alert Level 3; pyroclastic flows on 2 May
description: Mayon volcano entered a new eruption phase on 6 January 2026, prompting Alert Level 3 and a state of calamity in Tabaco, Albay. Pyroclastic flows on 2 May forced expanded evacuation zones across three cities and five municipalities. Activity subsided by early May.

name: Victoria Bushfires
scale: 400,000+ ha burned nationally; 140,000 ha in Longwood Fire alone
description: A series of severe bushfires burned across southeastern Australia in January 2026, with Victoria worst hit. The Longwood Fire alone consumed over 140,000 hectares. Nationally, five people died and nearly 400 homes were destroyed across Victoria, NSW, Tasmania, and Western Australia.

name: Cebu Landfill Collapse
scale: Landfill collapse burying employee building
description: The Binaliw landfill in Cebu City collapsed on 8 January 2026, burying an employee building and killing 36 people. A state of calamity was declared on 13 January as rescue operations continued.

name: Afghanistan Snowstorms
scale: 3-day nationwide blizzard
description: Three days of nationwide snowstorms killed at least 61 people across Afghanistan by 24 January 2026. The storms collapsed roofs, blocked roads, and cut off remote communities from relief supplies.

name: Chitral Avalanche
scale: Single large avalanche in mountainous terrain
description: An avalanche struck Chitral District in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province on 23 January 2026, killing nine people during a period of heavy winter snowfall across northern Pakistan.

name: West Bandung Landslide
scale: Debris field >2 km long, mud up to 8 m deep
cause: Heavy rainfall; land-use changes on Mount Burangrang
description: A massive landslide struck Pasirlangu village in Cisarua District at 02:30 local time on 24 January 2026, burying homes and a Marine Corps training exercise under mud up to 8 metres deep. Eighty people were confirmed dead and 20 remain missing. Among the victims were 23 Indonesian Marines. Some 2,100 rescue personnel worked the site until operations concluded on 14 February.

name: Minas Gerais Flash Floods
region: Juiz de Fora and Uba, Minas Gerais, Brazil
scale: Major flash flooding across two cities
description: Flash flooding struck the cities of Juiz de Fora and Uba in Minas Gerais state on 23 February 2026, killing at least 64 people with five others reported missing. The floods were the deadliest natural disaster in Brazil so far in 2026.

name: Kenya Deadly Floods
scale: Nationwide flooding over 3 weeks
description: Heavy rains triggered flooding across Kenya from early to late March 2026, killing at least 108 people. Nairobi was worst hit with 23 fatalities in the initial wave on 7 March. The death toll continued to climb through the month as rains persisted nationwide.

name: Cyclone Maila
region: Papua New Guinea and Solomon Islands
scale: Cat 5 (AU) / Cat 4 (SS); 205 km/h sustained, 929 hPa
displaced: Thousands across PNG and Solomon Islands
cause: Tropical cyclogenesis in the Coral Sea
description: Cyclone Maila was the strongest tropical cyclone in Port Moresby's area of responsibility on record. It formed on 1 April and peaked at Category 5 with 205 km/h sustained winds before tracking across the Solomon Sea. At least 25 people died, primarily from landslides in East New Britain and Bougainville in Papua New Guinea.

name: Super Typhoon Sinlaku
scale: Cat 5 equiv; 215 km/h (JMA), 295 km/h (JTWC), 890 hPa
description: Super Typhoon Sinlaku made landfall on Saipan on 14 April with sustained winds of 150 mph and over 20 inches of rainfall, collapsing the entire electrical grid on Saipan and Tinian. Total damages exceeded $1.55 billion, with the Northern Mariana Islands sustaining over $1 billion alone. Seventeen people died, including crew from an overturned cargo ship.

name: US April Tornado Outbreak
scale: 108 tornadoes confirmed; peak EF4 at Enid, Oklahoma
description: A major tornado outbreak from 23 to 28 April 2026 produced 108 confirmed tornadoes across the central United States. An EF4 tornado struck near Enid, Oklahoma on 23 April, destroying or flattening 40 homes and forcing the closure of Vance Air Force Base.

name: Hunan Fireworks Factory Explosion
scale: Factory-scale explosion
description: A fireworks factory explosion in Hunan province on 4 May 2026 killed at least 37 people. The blast was part of a pattern of fireworks-related industrial accidents in China during the first half of 2026.

name: Uttar Pradesh Deadly Rainstorms
scale: Statewide severe rainstorms
cause: Pre-monsoon severe thunderstorms and heavy rain
description: Severe rainstorms swept across Uttar Pradesh on 13 May 2026, killing at least 96 people. Deaths resulted from building collapses, lightning strikes, and flash flooding triggered by the intense downpours.

name: DR Congo Bundibugyo Ebola Epidemic
region: Ituri, North Kivu and five other provinces, DR Congo
scale: Largest Bundibugyo outbreak on record and second-largest Ebola outbreak; 62 health zones in 7 provinces; WHO PHEIC
casualties: 4,336 dead of 8,978 confirmed cases in DRC as of 11 Oct (Wikipedia, citing DRC INSP); 3,924 dead of 8,116 as of 27 Sep (UKHSA, citing WHO)
cause: Bundibugyo ebolavirus; likely seeded at a February 2026 funeral in Mongbwalu, Ituri
description: An Ebola outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain was confirmed in Ituri Province on 15 May 2026 and declared a public health emergency of international concern. By late September it covered 62 health zones in seven DRC provinces, with most cases in Ituri and a rise in North Kivu, and deaths passed 4,000 on 2 October. Uganda's 20-case spillover was declared over, and single cases reached Kenya and France. This is a gap-fill: the outbreak predates the window but was missing from the layer.

name: Shanxi Coal Mine Explosion
scale: Underground coal mine gas explosion
description: A gas explosion in a coal mine in Shanxi province on 22 May 2026 killed 82 miners, making it one of China's deadliest mining disasters in recent years. The blast occurred underground and trapped workers in the mine.

name: 2026 European Heat Waves
scale: 46.5 C peak (Noto, Sicily); multiple national records broken
description: Two successive heat waves struck Europe from late May through August 2026, killing an estimated 36,210 people. Germany was worst hit with 14,000 deaths, followed by France (7,300) and Spain (4,458). Noto, Sicily recorded 46.5 C on 22 July. Nuclear power plants shut down due to low river levels, roads melted, and widespread wildfires broke out. Total economic damage reached EUR 180 billion.

name: Canada 2026 Wildfire Season
scale: 4,492,283 ha burned; 5,248 fires (CIFFC, as of 31 Aug)
description: Canada's 2026 wildfire season burned over 4 million hectares by mid-August across Ontario, British Columbia, and Saskatchewan. The Thunder Bay 36 fire in Ontario alone consumed 318,813 hectares, one of the province's largest fires on record. British Columbia declared a province-wide state of emergency after the Bald Range fire forced 12,000 evacuations near Summerland.

name: Mindanao M7.8 Earthquake
scale: M7.8; thrust faulting; tsunami run-up 2.5 m
cause: Thrust faulting along the Cotabato Trench
description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck 25 km southwest of Kablalan, Sarangani at 07:37 local time on 8 June 2026, killing 107 people and injuring over 1,300. A tsunami with 2.5 m run-up reached Lebak, and warnings were issued for four countries. Coastal uplift of up to 2 metres was observed along 100 km of coastline. Economic losses reached $1.44 billion.

name: TS Arthur Texas/Gulf Floods
region: Gulf Coast, Texas and Louisiana, USA
scale: 45 mph sustained; 1-in-1,000-year rainfall; 29.06 in state record (LA)
cause: Tropical wave merging with remnant moisture
description: Tropical Storm Arthur made landfall near Galveston, Texas on 17 June 2026 and, despite weak winds, produced catastrophic 1-in-1,000-year rainfall. Louisiana recorded a new state rainfall record of 29.06 inches at Cottonport. The storm spawned 14 confirmed tornadoes across Louisiana and Mississippi. Total damages exceeded $1 billion.

name: Venezuela M7.5 Double Earthquake
region: La Guaira, Caracas, and central Venezuela
scale: M7.2 foreshock + M7.5 mainshock 30 s apart; depth 10 km
description: Two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela 30 seconds apart on 24 June 2026: a M7.2 foreshock near Yumare followed by the M7.5 mainshock off the coast of La Guaira. La Guaira saw 80% of buildings collapse. At least 6,509 people died, over 226,000 were injured, and 18,000-50,000 remain missing. Direct economic losses reached $37 billion, making it one of the deadliest earthquakes in the Western Hemisphere this century.

name: 2026 North American Heat Wave
scale: 46 C (115 F) in Miles City, MT; 41 C in Atlantic City, NJ; hottest July in US history
description: A series of heat domes produced the hottest July in American history, beginning on 28 June 2026. The eastern wave killed at least 44 people during 1-4 July, with Atlantic City reaching 41 C. A second western wave pushed Miles City, Montana to 46 C. Over 1.3 million power outages were reported across the continent.

name: Greece Wildfires
scale: Dozens of fires nationwide; helicopter collision near Athens
description: Multiple wildfires swept across Greece from late June through August 2026 during the broader European heat wave. At least 8 people died including two in a mid-air helicopter collision near Athens on 2 August. Thousands were evacuated from Crete, Thessaloniki, and the Attica region. Extensive agricultural and residential destruction was reported.

name: TS Maysak / Guangxi Floods
scale: 95 km/h sustained; dam breach in Nanning; EF3 tornado in Ezhou
displaced: 1.65 million affected in Guangxi; 3,600 evacuated in Vietnam
cause: Tropical storm triggering catastrophic inland flooding
description: Tropical Storm Maysak made landfall in Hainan on 3 July and Vietnam on 4 July, but its deadliest impact was catastrophic inland flooding in Guangxi province that killed 159 people, including 26 who died in a dam breach near Nanning. The system also spawned an EF3 tornado in Ezhou-Huanggang that killed 12 and injured 331. Total damages exceeded $3.35 billion.

name: Gansu Tanchang Landslide
scale: Landslide burying forestry crew
description: A landslide in Tanchang County, Gansu province on 7 July 2026 killed 21 forestry workers. The slide was triggered by heavy rainfall in the mountainous terrain of western China.

name: Quanzhou Factory Fire
scale: Large shoe factory fire
description: A fire at a shoe factory in Quanzhou, Fujian province on 9 July 2026 killed 28 workers. The blaze was one of several deadly industrial fires in China during the year.

name: Bangladesh Monsoon Floods
scale: Nationwide flooding from prolonged monsoon rains
description: Days of heavy monsoon rainfall caused nationwide flooding across Bangladesh, killing at least 51 people by 13 July 2026. Multiple regions experienced river overflow and inundation of low-lying areas.

name: Chongqing Pengshui Landslide
scale: Large landslide burying settlement
description: A major landslide in Pengshui County, Chongqing municipality on 17 July 2026 left 61 people dead or missing. The slide was triggered by torrential rain that destabilised slopes above the settlement.

name: 2026 Assam Floods
region: Upper Assam (Sivasagar, Charaideo, Jorhat, Golaghat), India
scale: 4 rivers above danger level; 481 villages submerged; 10,748 ha cropland flooded
cause: Cloudburst in Nagaland hills; deforestation and mining
description: Catastrophic flooding struck upper Assam from 19 July onwards after a cloudburst in neighbouring Nagaland. The Dikhow, Disang, Janji, and Dhansiri rivers all crossed danger levels, submerging 481 villages and displacing over 700,000 people. More than 100 people died and 10,748 hectares of cropland were destroyed. The floods remained ongoing as of mid-August 2026. By 8 August the waters were receding: 155,000 people were still affected and damage assessment began on 9 August.

name: Sikkim Tunnel Collapse
scale: Under-construction tunnel methane explosion and collapse
cause: Methane gas explosion in under-construction tunnel
description: A methane gas explosion caused the collapse of an under-construction tunnel in Sikkim on 20 July 2026, killing 25 workers and injuring 13 others. Rescue operations recovered the bodies over several days.

name: Kumamoto M6.8 Earthquake
scale: M6.8 (Mw) / M7.1 (JMA); depth 16 km; surface ruptures ~10 km
description: A magnitude 6.8 earthquake struck 5 km east of Uto, Kumamoto Prefecture at 16:27 local time on 28 July 2026, killing 38 people and injuring over 368. Nine people died when a paper factory chimney collapsed, and the Aeon Mall Kumamoto partially collapsed followed by an LPG explosion. Kumamoto Castle sustained further damage. Total losses reached $738 million.

name: Broad Peak Avalanche
scale: High-altitude avalanche on 8,051 m peak
description: An avalanche on Broad Peak in Gilgit-Baltistan on 30 July 2026 killed four climbers and left six others missing on the world's twelfth-highest mountain.

name: California Bug Fire
region: Lassen and Sierra Counties, CA / Washoe County, NV, USA
scale: 93,733 acres (37,930 ha): 12,817 in California, 80,916 in Nevada
casualties: 1 dead (civilian on the Nevada side, burn injuries sustained 12 Aug)
displaced: Evacuations near Cold Springs and Reno Stead Airport
description: The Bug Fire ignited on 8 August 2026 in Lassen and Sierra counties and grew to become California's largest fire of the year at 93,733 acres, crossing into Washoe County, Nevada near the Reno area. The fire prompted evacuations near Cold Springs and the Reno Stead Airport. The state's extreme heat and snowpack at just 18% of average fuelled an aggressive fire season.

name: Colombia M7.4 Earthquake
scale: M7.4; depth 110 km; felt in Ecuador and Panama
cause: Strike-slip faulting within subducting Nazca plate
description: A magnitude 7.4 earthquake struck 20 km from San Jose del Palmar in Choco Department at 07:34 local time on 10 August 2026. The tremor was felt across western and central Colombia and into Ecuador and Panama. At least 331 people died, over 4,600 were injured, and 31,540 homes were destroyed. The Colombian government declared a national emergency with estimated economic losses of $9.6 billion.

name: Flores M7.7 Earthquake
scale: M7.7; depth 10 km; tsunami 1.61 m at Reok
cause: Shallow thrust faulting off Flores's northern coast
description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck 68 km north-northwest of Ende off Flores's coast at 05:58 local time on 15 August 2026. It killed 111 people, injured 1,678, and displaced over 185,000. A tsunami warning was issued within 2 minutes, and a 1.61 m wave reached Reok. Nearly 78,000 homes and 1,378 schools were damaged. It was Indonesia's deadliest earthquake since 2022.

name: Nepal-Tibet Glacial Collapse
region: Rasuwa and Nuwakot Districts, Nepal / Gyirong, Tibet, China
scale: Hundreds of millions of tonnes of rock and ice from ~5,200 m; flood wave 40-50 m high at ~70 km/h; seismic signal equivalent to M5.2
casualties: 1,498 dead, 5,804 missing (Nepal 1,455 dead / 5,285 missing per NDRRMA, 3 Oct; Tibet 43 dead / 519 missing, 18 Sep)
displaced: Tens of thousands; 19 bridges, ~40 km road destroyed
cause: Glacier tongue sheared off when underlying rock failed; accelerated by permafrost thaw and climate-driven glacial retreat
description: On 26 August 2026 at 02:55 UTC, the lower tongue of a glacier near Langtang Lirung (7,227 m) sheared off at approximately 5,200 m elevation when the underlying rock failed, sending hundreds of millions of tonnes of ice and rock plunging 2,200 m into the Lhende Khola valley on the Tibet side of the border. The mass dammed the river; when the blockage breached, a wall of water estimated at 40-50 m high travelling at roughly 70 km/h tore through settlements in Nepal's Rasuwa district, destroying Timure and much of Syapru Besi, sweeping away 19 bridges, hydropower plants, and approximately 40 km of road. The toll rose for weeks as bodies were recovered down the Trishuli: by early October Nepal counted 1,455 dead and 5,285 missing, hundreds of them foreign visitors, and halted search and rescue on 5 October; Tibet reported 43 dead and 519 missing. Nepal put reconstruction at NPR 559 bn (about US$3.6 bn). The seismic signal registered M5.2 on USGS instruments, and researchers warned that permafrost thaw and accelerating glacial melt make such collapses increasingly likely.

name: Grand Canyon Bright Angel Flash Flood
region: Bright Angel Canyon / Phantom Ranch, Arizona, USA
scale: Flash flood through Bright Angel Canyon to the Colorado River; 82 people rescued
casualties: 2 dead; ~12-15 unaccounted for in early reports, later cut to 1 missing
displaced: 82 rescued from the inner canyon, most by helicopter
cause: Intense monsoon thunderstorm rainfall over the Bright Angel Creek drainage
description: A flash flood tore through Bright Angel Canyon and the Phantom Ranch area of Grand Canyon National Park on 29 August 2026. At least two people died, and the National Park Service first listed about 15 people as missing or unaccounted for; later reports put it at one. 82 people were rescued, and the flood destroyed inner-canyon footbridges and damaged the Transcanyon Waterline.

name: Jiangxi Suichuan Mudslides
scale: Series of rain-triggered mudslides and landslides; 18,000+ evacuated
cause: Days of heavy rain; Wikipedia attributes the first Suichuan mudslide to the remnants of Typhoon Saudel (inference on linkage)
description: Several days of heavy rain set off a series of mudslides and landslides in Suichuan County, Jiangxi, including at Mingkeng village. By 10 September authorities had confirmed 16 dead, and more than 18,000 residents had been evacuated. The 2026 Pacific typhoon season article ties the initial Suichuan mudslide (1 dead, 11 missing) to Typhoon Saudel, which made its last landfall in Fujian on 3 September; the exact start date is approximate.

name: Hurricane Lowell Strikes Kauai and Niihau
scale: Peak Cat 5 (160 mph, 922 mbar); center passed ~64 km W of Niihau; first tornado watch on record for Hawaii
displaced: 18 homes destroyed, 100+ major damage, 700+ damaged (Kauai County, 18 Sep)
cause: Eastern/Central Pacific hurricane recurving north past the western Hawaiian Islands
description: Hurricane Lowell, which peaked at Category 5, passed about 64 km west of Niihau on 8 September 2026 and gave Kauai and Niihau a direct hit. Three people died: one on Kauai from storm surge, one in Wainiha, and one on Oahu when a tree fell on a tent. More than 91% of Kauai County lost power. Governor Josh Green said damage would exceed $400 million, with early estimates of $500 million to $1 billion, and compared the blow to Iniki.

name: Thailand and Bangkok Floods
region: Bangkok and 21+ provinces (Prachin Buri, Samut Prakan, Nakhon Nayok), Thailand
scale: 3.13 million+ people affected across 21 provinces and parts of Bangkok; damage est. >฿11 bn (~$320-367 m)
casualties: 44 dead (AFP, 8 Oct): Prachin Buri 19, Samut Prakan 9, Nakhon Nayok 4, Bangkok 4
displaced: Thousands in Bangkok shelters; ~700,000 affected in the capital (DDPM)
cause: Monsoon rains plus a deep depression (BOB 07) moving inland over Thailand in late September
description: Flooding that began on 16 September 2026 spread across central and eastern Thailand and into Bangkok in late September, when a deep depression moved inland. By 29 September the government counted 23 dead, four of them in Bangkok, and DDPM reported 2.6 million people affected. AFP put the toll at 44 dead and over 3.13 million affected on 8 October. Reuters cited damage estimates above $320 million.

name: Typhoon Dujuan Landslides in Kanto
region: Chiba, Kanagawa (Yokosuka, Miura), Izu Oshima, Japan
scale: Typhoon, 140 km/h 10-min peak; 832 mm in 48 h on Izu Oshima (record since 1991)
casualties: 6 dead (5 Chiba, 1 Kanagawa), 6 missing, 22+ injured (22 Sep)
displaced: 1.6 million+ under evacuation orders (Wikipedia season table)
cause: Typhoon rainfall triggering landslides on saturated slopes
description: Typhoon Dujuan brushed the Kanto region on 21-22 September 2026 and dropped a record 832 mm of rain in 48 hours on Izu Oshima. Landslides in Kanagawa and Chiba killed six people and left six missing, mostly around Yokosuka and Miura, and at least 22 were injured. Tens of thousands of homes lost power.

name: Uttar Pradesh Retreating-Monsoon Floods
region: Uttar Pradesh (statewide), with Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, India
scale: Very heavy rain in nearly all 75 UP districts; 2,254 houses damaged; 15,000+ evacuated in Odisha
casualties: 81 dead, 62 injured in Uttar Pradesh; Wikipedia's BOB 06 total adds 19 in Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh
displaced: 15,000+ evacuated in Odisha; UP displacement not reported
cause: Deep depression BOB 06 (JTWC 01B) crossing the south Odisha / north Andhra coast and tracking inland during monsoon withdrawal
description: Deep Depression BOB 06 formed over the Bay of Bengal on 21 September 2026 and moved inland, bringing three days of extreme rain to Uttar Pradesh around 25-28 September. UP's Relief Commissioner reported 81 dead, 62 injured, more than 2,200 houses damaged and 154 animals killed. More than 15,000 people were evacuated in Odisha, and the same system fed deadly floods in Nepal.

name: Nepal Kali Gandaki Landslides and Floods
region: Mustang, Baglung, Myagdi, Manang, Palpa (Gandaki/Lumbini), Nepal
scale: Mountainside collapse into the Kali Gandaki River; Syangja-Gulmi bridge swept away; 144 MW Kali Gandaki A plant shut
casualties: At least 24 dead, 14 missing (28 Sep); Wikipedia later tallies 31 flood/landslide deaths + 15 in a Manang avalanche
displaced: ~1,500 people (435 households) in Gandaki Province; 747 families affected
cause: Days of heavy rain from the remnants of Deep Depression BOB 06 during monsoon withdrawal
description: After days of heavy rain, part of a mountain in Mustang District collapsed into the Kali Gandaki River on 27 September 2026, and floods and landslides struck across western Nepal. At least 24 people died, including 10 in Baglung and 6 in Myagdi, and 14 were missing. An avalanche on Himlung Himal in Manang killed climbers. About 1,500 people were displaced, a bridge between Syangja and Gulmi was swept away, and the Kali Gandaki A hydropower plant halted.
sources: Wikipedia 2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_North_Indian_Ocean_cyclone_season

name: Yaroslavl Pyrotechnics Plant Fire and Blast
region: Kubrinsk, Pereslavl District, Yaroslavl Oblast, Russia
scale: Fire and explosions at a pyrotechnics plant/warehouse (Salyut Yug LLC); 9 apartment buildings damaged
casualties: 14 dead (Emergencies Ministry via TASS); others reported missing
cause: Fire at a pyrotechnics facility; short circuit presumed (Investigative Committee, per Charter 97), cause disputed
description: On 28 September 2026 a fire and explosions at a pyrotechnics plant in Kubrinsk, Yaroslavl region, killed 14 people, according to TASS and the Emergencies Ministry. The blast damaged nine nearby apartment buildings and cut power to the village. Investigators opened a criminal case over safety violations and detained the plant's director, and the governor declared 30 September a day of mourning. Coordinates are those of Pereslavl-Zalessky, the district seat, not the plant itself.

name: Panama M7.7 Azuero Earthquake
scale: Mw 7.7 strike-slip; depth 12.6 km; MMI IX at Tonosí; Mw 6.6 aftershock; felt by 4.5 million
displaced: 2,097 structures damaged or destroyed (SINAPROC); 300 evacuated from Isla de Cañas
cause: Shallow strike-slip faulting off the Azuero Peninsula
description: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck the southern Azuero Peninsula at 12:56 local time on 9 October 2026. It was Panama's strongest since 1882, and a Mw 6.6 aftershock followed two and a half hours later. At least 27 people were injured and SINAPROC counted 2,097 structures damaged or destroyed; a hotel and homes collapsed in Tonosí, and outages hit six provinces. A regional tsunami warning was issued, but no damaging tsunami was reported.

name: Hurricane Isaias Landfall Near Destin
region: Florida Panhandle (Okaloosa, Escambia) and Alabama, USA
scale: Landfall as Cat 2 (~105 mph) after Cat 3 peak (120 mph); ~900,000 customers without power
casualties: 4-5 dead (2 FL, 2 AL per Euronews/AP; Wikipedia adds 1 in SC)
cause: Atlantic hurricane making Gulf Coast landfall
description: Hurricane Isaias came ashore near Destin, Florida, late on 9 October local time (01:30 UTC on 10 October) as a Category 2 storm, after peaking at Category 3. Nearly 900,000 customers lost power across Florida and Alabama. Winds tore the roof off a Pensacola hotel and damaged a Panama City Beach high-rise. At least four deaths were reported in Florida and Alabama, and Wikipedia lists a fifth in South Carolina.
